newsitem.title: USA: Mobil says has 50 pct of Azeri block.
newsitem.headline: Mobil says has 50 pct of Azeri block.

text.p: Mobil Corp said Friday that it has a 50 percent share and will operate the Oguz block in Azerbaijan under the deal it signed with the Azeri president in Washington.
"Under the terms of the (production sharing agreement) PSA, Mobil will be the operator with a 50 percent working interest in the block," Mobil said in a statement.

"SOCAR will hold the remaining interest. The PSA calls for exploration drilling to be completed on the block over the next three years. Mobil is also negotiating with SOCAR on obtaining rights to other projects in Azerbaijan," the statement said.
The deal was signed at the White House Friday during a state visit of His Excellency Heydar A. Aliev, President of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

Oguz is a 56,100 acre (227 square kilometers) block located approximately 61 miles (100 kilometers) east of Baku near the Oil Rocks and Guneshli oil fields on the prolific Absheron Trend, offshore Azerbaijan.

"This new venture is a major step forward for Mobil in building its long-term exploration and producing business in Azerbaijan and supports our strategy to make the Caspian region a core producing area," said M.W. Scoggins, President of Mobil's New Exploration and Producing Ventures and Global Exploration.
Oguz may have 40 million tonnes of recoverable crude oil reserves, Azerbaijan state oil company SOCAR has estimated.
A Mobil spokesman said the company did not yet have an estimate for recoverable crude from the block.
Three other deals were signed Friday with Exxon Corp , Chevron Corp and Amoco Corp.
